questions.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ by inspection.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{2}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{2}=2\cdot {a}_{1}+0\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{2}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is spanned by just ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}},{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Basis of the Space Spanned by a Set of Vectors by Identifying Pivot Columns
questions.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, our matrix is already in a row echelon form.

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}.
$$

questions.problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],$ ${a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 16\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$

We need to find a subset of linearly independent vectors. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}3 & 12 & 6 \\ 4 & 16 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 4 & 16 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $3$rd columns are pivot columns, while the $2$nd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one.

The $1$st and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Given Set Is a Basis of a Span
questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are given below. Determine whether $B={{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ where ${a}_{3}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -10\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -10\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-6 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-10\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -6 \\ 1 & 2 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the RREF matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=-4,$ meaning that

$$
(-2)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+(-4)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}={{[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -10\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=(-2)\cdot (-4)=8.$

questions.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1},$ ${a}_{2},$ ${a}_{3},$ and ${a}_{4}$ are given below. Determine whether $B={{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3},$ where ${a}_{4}={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -29 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -29 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=-9 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=-29 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -9 \\ 3 & 4 & 6 & -29 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{2}=-2,$ and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ meaning that

$$
(-1)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+(-2)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+(-3)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -29 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=(-1)+(-2)+(-3)=-6.$

{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$ So, we want to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+{x}_{2}{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+{x}_{3}{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ 5{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & -2 & 2 \\ 5 & -5 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -5 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $B$ is indeed a basis of $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3},{a}_{4}}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that ${x}_{1}=-8,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=7,$ meaning that

$$
(-8)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}}+0\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{2}}+7\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}={{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{4}}.
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-8+0+7=-1.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that $\mathbf{a}_2$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_3\mathbin{:}$

$$
\mathbf{a}_2=1\cdot \mathbf{a}_1+1\cdot \mathbf{a}_3
$$

Consequently, the vector $\mathbf{a}_2$ can be removed from $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3 \}$ without changing the span. So $S = \textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3 \}$ is spanned by just $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_3\}.$ 

Lastly, note that $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_3\}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_3\},$ that is to say,

Determine whether $\mathcal{B} = \{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3 \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3, \mathbf{a}_4 \}.$ If that is the case, find $x_1 + x_2 + x_3,$ where $\mathbf{a}_4=x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We want to determine if $\mathcal{B}$ is indeed a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3,\mathbf{a}_4 \}.$ So, we want to find $x_1, x_2, x_3 \in \mathbb{R}$ such that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064318/assets/a23531cb53a9b53f47d8a7080af7de78e6d7cdd7fa3a3632c37a720c7e8ba92c.png)

This equation is equivalent to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3}=2 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we reduce the augmented matrix of the system to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the reduced matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns. So,  $\mathcal{B}$ is indeed a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3,\mathbf{a}_4 \}.$
Also, the matrix tells us that $x_1=-5,$ $x_2=0,$ and $x_3=7,$ meaning that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064318/assets/ca123e2e8451fab6c7b106a5d1a05d153020854c694ec41cfb5d38de2fb3ae5f.png)

Therefore, $x_1 + x_2 +  x_3 = (-5) + 0 + 7 = 2.$
